name: GA-08
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbent Austin Scott seeking re-election with large financial edge
Democratic challenger Kelly Esti has raised only ~$19K with minimal cash
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~94%
model.rationale: Austin Scott holds a heavily Republican seat, has a massive fundraising advantage, and faces an underfunded first-time challenger with no polling or outside spending to suggest a competitive race. Markets and fundamentals both point to a comfortable Republican win.
model.watch: Any late surge in Democratic fundraising or outside spending, or a major scandal involving the incumbent, could narrow the race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Georgia's 8th District leans strongly Republican, with a partisan baseline of about R+15. Incumbent Austin Scott is running for re-election and has raised over $1.1 million with $1.3 million on hand. His Democratic challenger, Kelly Esti, has raised under $20,000 and reports minimal cash, leaving her with little capacity to compete.

No polls or expert ratings cover this race, and prediction markets give Scott roughly a 94% chance of winning. With no outside spending targeting the district and no evidence of a competitive environment, the seat is expected to remain comfortably in Republican hands.
